articles.title: American Vlogger Tries Kulfi for the First Time in Amritsar, Gives It a Perfect 10
articles.excerpt: Content creator AJ Elizarde discovers India's dense, slow-cooked frozen dessert at a street stall in Punjab and can't stop praising its nutty, milky complexity.
articles.image_caption: Traditional Indian kulfi. An American vlogger gave the frozen dessert a perfect score of 10 after trying it for the first time in Amritsar.
articles.nri_angle: Kulfi reaction videos resonate with diaspora Indians who miss street food experiences that are difficult to replicate abroad, even with store-bought kulfi brands.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Kolkata Goes Beyond Idli-Dosa With Malabari Biryani, Chettinad Chicken and Banana-Leaf Feasts
articles.excerpt: Two major hotel food festivals in the city spotlight lesser-known dishes from Kerala, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu, serving everything from kaima-rice biryani to banana flower fritters.
articles.nri_angle: The broadening of South Indian cuisine beyond idli-dosa in Indian cities mirrors a trend already visible in diaspora restaurants across the Bay Area, London and Toronto.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: How To Make Instant Dosa: The South Indian Classic Without Overnight Fermentation
articles.excerpt: A combination of rice flour, semolina, yogurt and baking soda delivers crisp, golden dosas in under 30 minutes — no soaking or waiting required.
articles.image_caption: A freshly made dosa served on a plate. The South Indian classic can be made without overnight fermentation using an instant batter method.
articles.nri_angle: Instant dosa offers diaspora Indians a practical way to enjoy a South Indian breakfast staple on busy weekday mornings without overnight preparation.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: High-Protein Paneer Tikka: A Gym-Friendly Take on the Classic Indian Starter
articles.excerpt: This tandoori-style paneer tikka delivers up to 25 grams of protein per serving using low-fat paneer, hung curd and minimal oil.
articles.nri_angle: A protein-optimized take on a beloved Indian starter, designed for health-conscious diaspora cooks balancing fitness goals with familiar flavors.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Viral Video of Family Eating on Rajasthan Expressway Sparks Debate, but Context Tells a Different Story
articles.excerpt: A video of a family dining on a newly inaugurated expressway drew outrage, but closer inspection suggests they were at an empty lay-by with no facilities — not trespassing on live traffic lanes.
articles.nri_angle: The viral clip resonated with NRIs who recognize the gap between India's rapid infrastructure expansion and the on-the-ground travel experience their families navigate.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: How To Make Milk Peda: A Classic Indian Sweet With Mathura Roots
articles.excerpt: This simple recipe uses milk powder and condensed milk to recreate the beloved temple sweet in under 30 minutes, no traditional khoya required.
articles.nri_angle: Peda is a staple at Indian sweet shops and festival celebrations across the diaspora, and this home recipe connects kitchens abroad to the Mathura temple tradition.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: How To Make Dhaniya Panjiri for Janmashtami in Under 15 Minutes
articles.excerpt: This traditional coriander-based prasad, made with ghee, dry fruits, and roasted spices, is one of the simplest and most beloved offerings for Lord Krishna's birthday.
articles.image_caption: Dhaniya panjiri, a traditional Janmashtami prasad made with roasted coriander, dry fruits, and sugar.
articles.nri_angle: Panjiri is one of the easiest Janmashtami preparations to replicate abroad, needing only Indian grocery staples.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Elderly Couple's Steel-Plate Paratha Meal on Flight Goes Viral, Reignites Homemade Food Debate
articles.excerpt: A photo of an older couple eating chapatis, sabzi and Amul dahi from a steel thali mid-flight has drawn millions of views and mixed reactions — the latest in a string of viral Indian in-flight food moments.
articles.image_caption: An elderly couple eats homemade chapatis, sabzi and Amul dahi from a steel plate during a flight. The image, posted on X by Nalini Unagar on August 30, has gone viral with millions of views.
articles.nri_angle: The viral moment reflects a deeply Indian travel tradition — packing ghar ka khana for every journey. For the diaspora, the steel thali and Amul dahi packet are instantly recognizable cultural markers, evoking memories of family trips and home-cooked meals that no airline menu can replace.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Sooji or Aata? A Nutritionist Settles the Great Golgappa Shell Debate
articles.excerpt: When choosing between semolina and whole-wheat golgappa shells, aata offers a nutritional edge — but the bigger win is keeping them an occasional treat.
articles.image_caption: Golgappa, also known as panipuri or puchka, the popular Indian street snack. A nutritionist weighs in on whether sooji or whole-wheat aata shells are the healthier choice.
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora families making golgappas at home, choosing the right shell ingredients is entirely in their hands.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Twinkle Khanna and Dimple Kapadia Are Making Paneer at Home. The Fake Paneer Crisis Made Them Do It.
articles.excerpt: The author and her mother have turned to homemade paneer amid India's growing food adulteration scandal, sparking a family rivalry over whose kitchen produces more.
articles.image_caption: Author and former actress Twinkle Khanna. She and her mother, veteran actress Dimple Kapadia, have started making paneer at home in response to India's fake paneer crisis.
articles.nri_angle: For Indian families abroad, homemade paneer has always been standard practice, making the paneer crisis particularly relatable.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: From Street Food Vendors to Italian Nonnas: How Indian Wedding Menus Became Personal
articles.excerpt: The grand 100-dish buffet is giving way to curated, story-driven menus — couples are flying in favourite chaatwallas, recreating first-date dishes, and turning wedding meals into edible biographies.
articles.image_caption: A modern Indian wedding food spread. Couples are increasingly personalizing their menus with everything from street food vendors to international cuisines.
articles.nri_angle: Diaspora weddings are at the forefront of this trend, with NRI couples drawing on cuisines from countries they have lived in and foods that trace their cross-cultural journeys.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Chef Kunal Kapur's Moong Dal Idli With Smoky Tomato Chutney Is the Breakfast Upgrade You Need
articles.excerpt: Light, protein-packed, and naturally gluten-free, this golden idli recipe swaps traditional rice batter for soaked moong dal — with a charred tomato chutney that ties it all together.
articles.image_caption: Moong dal idli, a protein-rich variation of the classic South Indian steamed cake. Chef Kunal Kapur's recipe replaces traditional rice-and-urad batter with soaked skinless moong dal.
articles.nri_angle: A high-protein, gluten-free breakfast option from a top Indian chef that uses pantry staples available in most Indian grocery stores abroad.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Six Chennai Restaurants Keeping Karnataka's Tiffin Tradition Alive
articles.excerpt: From Woodlands' legendary rava idli to Tiffin Shastra's Darshini-style service, the city's vegetarian scene draws deeply from its cross-border culinary roots.
articles.image_caption: A spread of South Indian tiffin items. Six restaurants in Chennai are keeping alive Karnataka's traditional tiffin culture with recipes rooted in the state's culinary heritage.
articles.nri_angle: A guide for diaspora foodies and travelers looking for authentic South Indian vegetarian dining beyond the standard dosa in Chennai.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Beyond Dal Tadka: Six Regional Masala Dals Every Indian Home Cook Should Know
articles.excerpt: From Punjab's slow-cooked langarwali dal to Maharashtra's sweet-tangy amti, India's regional lentil traditions offer far more depth and variety than the standard restaurant tadka.
articles.image_caption: A spread of regional Indian dals in earthen bowls. India offers dozens of distinct lentil preparations shaped by local spice blends, available ingredients, and cooking traditions.
articles.nri_angle: For NRI home cooks who grew up with dal as a daily staple, exploring regional variations offers a way to reconnect with India's culinary diversity and expand a comfort-food repertoire that often defaults to the same two or three recipes.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Air India Adds Wood-Fired Pizzas to In-Flight Menu on Select US-India Routes
articles.excerpt: The stone-baked option is now available in Economy and Premium Economy on five North America routes as part of the airline's ongoing dining overhaul.
articles.image_caption: Air India has introduced stone-baked, wood-fired pizzas on select long-haul flights between North America and India. The new option is available in Economy and Premium Economy cabins on five routes.
articles.nri_angle: Air India's North American routes are among the most traveled by the Indian diaspora, making in-flight food quality a frequent topic of discussion in the NRI community.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Inside Nagpur's Saoji Cuisine: The 150-Year-Old Tradition Behind India's Spiciest Mutton Curry
articles.excerpt: Born in the kitchens of Halba Koshti weavers who migrated to Nagpur in 1877, Saoji food uses a closely guarded 32-spice masala and is now spreading from central India to Japan.
articles.image_caption: A mutton curry from Nagpur, Maharashtra. The 150-year-old Saoji cuisine tradition originated with Halba Koshti weavers who migrated to the city in the 1870s.
articles.nri_angle: Saoji cuisine connects NRIs from Nagpur and Vidarbha to their regional food identity, while a Japanese chef's embrace of the tradition highlights Indian cuisine's growing global reach.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Chef Arun Vijayan Decodes Kerala's Gentle Spice Philosophy at Kolkata Pop-Up
articles.excerpt: A traditional Kerala cuisine pop-up at Fairfield by Marriott, Kolkata, showcases the state's lighter, milder approach to spices — and why it stands apart from the rest of South India.
articles.image_caption: A traditional Kerala sadya meal served on a banana leaf. Chef Arun Vijayan brought Kerala's gentle spice philosophy to a pop-up event in Kolkata.
articles.nri_angle: Kerala cuisine's gentle spice philosophy offers a different perspective for diaspora cooks accustomed to the heat of other South Indian regional styles.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: How to Make Palak Kofta at Home: The Classic Shaam Savera Recipe Simplified
articles.excerpt: Paneer-stuffed spinach dumplings in a smooth onion-tomato-cashew gravy — a show-stopping North Indian dish made without butter or cream.
articles.image_caption: Halved palak kofta dumplings sit in a smooth orange onion-tomato gravy, showing the dark green spinach exterior and white paneer center. The contrast gives the dish its name Shaam Savera, meaning evening and dawn.
articles.nri_angle: Palak Kofta is a show-stopping dish that NRI families can make at home for special occasions, bringing the flavors of North Indian restaurant cooking into diaspora kitchens.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian Restaurant Samudhra Signs 10,000-Square-Foot Lease Near Times Square
articles.excerpt: The Franklin Park, New Jersey-based premium Indian restaurant and lounge will open its first Manhattan location at The Ellery, a luxury mixed-use tower in Hell's Kitchen.
articles.image_caption: Times Square in New York City. Indian restaurant Samudhra has signed a 10,000-square-foot lease near the iconic intersection, marking one of the largest Indian dining spaces in Manhattan.
articles.nri_angle: An Indian-American entrepreneur's leap from New Jersey's diaspora dining scene to one of Manhattan's most competitive retail corridors reflects the growing mainstream appeal of premium Indian cuisine in the U.S.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: American YouTuber Ed Nathanson Says Indian Food Has 'Literally Ruined' All Other Cuisines for Him
articles.excerpt: The self-proclaimed 'World's Greatest Snack Detective' says discovering pani puri, chicken vindaloo, and gobi Manchurian five years ago permanently changed his palate — and his viral video has Indian food lovers inviting him to visit India.
articles.image_caption: A spread of Indian dishes. American YouTuber Ed Nathanson went viral for declaring Indian food has 'literally ruined' all other cuisines for him.
articles.nri_angle: Indian food gaining mainstream global recognition validates diaspora cultural identity, and viral moments like these boost visibility and foot traffic for Indian restaurants across the US.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Sweeping Food Safety Crackdown Hits Quick Commerce Giants and Liquor Makers
articles.excerpt: Maharashtra's food safety chief has suspended permits at Blinkit, Swiggy, and Zepto warehouses while FSSAI bans popular Diageo and Inbrew spirits for artificial flavouring, marking India's most aggressive enforcement push in years.
articles.image_caption: An FSSAI inspection. India's food safety regulator has launched a sweeping crackdown on quick commerce platforms and liquor manufacturers over labeling and hygiene violations.
articles.nri_angle: India's food safety crackdown on quick commerce warehouses and alcohol brands affects products consumed by millions, including the diaspora market for Indian-made liquor exports.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Chef Vikas Khanna Raises Funds and Spirits at Atlanta Gala for Leap to Shine
articles.excerpt: The Michelin-starred chef and 2026 TIME100 honoree headlined an intimate fundraising dinner in Atlanta to support digital education for underserved children across India
articles.nri_angle: Indian-American chef Vikas Khanna leverages his global platform to mobilize the NRI community around education access in India, raising funds at an Atlanta gala that highlights the diaspora's role in bridging opportunities for underserved children back home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Egg Prices Hit Record Highs as Ethanol Push Squeezes Poultry Feed Supply
articles.excerpt: Maize diversion to biofuel and soaring soybean costs create a twin feed shock, with retail prices up 40 percent and branded eggs expected to reach Rs 20-25
articles.nri_angle: Rising egg prices affect families in India who depend on eggs as affordable protein; diaspora members sending remittances feel the impact of food inflation on household budgets
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Proposes Red Warning Labels on Packaged Food After Supreme Court Pressure
articles.excerpt: FSSAI reverses course to mandate hexagonal warning symbols for high sugar, fat, and salt products in a setback for Coca-Cola, Nestle, and PepsiCo
articles.nri_angle: Indian diaspora families who regularly send or receive packaged food from India will be directly affected; those living abroad are familiar with warning labels and question why India lacks them
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Sanjeev Kapoor Shares Sugar-Free Multigrain Crackers Recipe Using Ragi, Jowar, and Bajra
articles.excerpt: The Padma Shri-awarded chef's air-fried cracker recipe uses three traditional Indian millets and zero sugar, offering a healthy alternative to packaged snacks.
articles.image_caption: Celebrity chef Sanjeev Kapoor, who shared a sugar-free multigrain crackers recipe using ragi, jowar, and bajra.
articles.nri_angle: Ragi, jowar, and bajra flours are now widely available at Indian grocery stores in the US, making this health-conscious recipe accessible for diaspora families.

articles.title: How to Make Chef Ranveer Brar's Kashmiri Chicken Kathi Roll at Home
articles.excerpt: The celebrity chef's 30-minute recipe pairs spice-marinated chicken thighs with two homemade chutneys, wrapped in a soft roti that traces its roots to Kolkata's Nizam's restaurant.
articles.nri_angle: A home-friendly recipe that lets diaspora cooks recreate an iconic Indian street food with Kashmiri regional flavours often unavailable outside India.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
